explanation: Map each binary counter value i to i XOR (i shifted right once). This reflected Gray-code mapping visits every bit pattern once and changes one bit between consecutive outputs.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space, plus O(2^b) output space.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The map g(i)=i XOR (i>>1) is invertible on b-bit values, so all 2^b outputs are distinct. Consecutive binary values differ by a carry run; XORing each with its right shift cancels that run except at one bit, giving consecutive Gray values Hamming distance one.
walkthrough: For 3 bits, i=0..7 maps to [0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4]. For example 3 XOR 2 = 1 and 2 XOR 6 = 4, each a single set bit. All eight values occur exactly once.
edgeCases: Zero bits gives the single value [0].
Do not repeat a pattern or use values outside the b-bit range.
The output has exponential size even though each value is computed in constant word operations.
